scientific_question: Does answer-conditioned c_fc temporal-state recovery cross the existing gates at a still-credible procedural budget, or only after coefficient and support storage becomes dense-scale?

budget_interpretation.six_stages: 17.1875% of dense scalar count; 25.78125% of dense bytes after adding the minimum uint16 support payload.
budget_interpretation.twelve_stages: 34.375% of dense scalar count; 51.5625% of dense bytes after adding the minimum uint16 support payload.
budget_interpretation.eighteen_stages: 51.5625% of dense scalar count; 77.34375% of dense bytes after minimum support storage and therefore classified as dense-scale for this project.
budget_interpretation.twenty_four_stages: 68.75% of dense scalar count; 103.125% of dense bytes after minimum support storage, already larger than the dense FP32 state.
budget_interpretation.thirty_stages: 85.9375% of dense scalar count; 128.90625% of dense bytes after minimum support storage.

interpretation_contract.moderate_pass: Both state families first pass by 12 stages. This establishes only terminal codability and authorizes a separately preregistered temporal-causality acquisition, not an optimizer candidate.
interpretation_contract.dense_scale_pass: Both families pass only after 12 stages. Widening is rejected as a credible state-compression fix because minimum coefficient-plus-support storage is at least 77.34% of dense state.
interpretation_contract.no_pass: At least one family still fails at 30 stages. The actual directed-product family is structurally misaligned with the temporal state even at a code larger than dense storage after supports.
interpretation_contract.no_training: Every outcome is a zero-update accounting/geometry result. No model training or larger rung is authorized.
